contradicting_evidence: Improving ETH/BTC and modestly better breadth could precede stabilization if sustained, although neither currently confirms recovery.
The latest settled BTC ETF session recorded a $7.9 million inflow, offsetting some bearish flow interpretation; ETH recorded an $8.4 million outflow.
Large-alt proxy median performance was less negative than BTC, showing that weakness is not uniform across capitalization buckets.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: A downside-biased, uneven path is favored: rebounds may occur, but sustained recovery faces weak participation and contracting liquidity. Confidence is low because a short observation sequence cannot establish multi-day persistence. Relative altcoin strength should not be interpreted as a confirmed rotation.
falsification_conditions: BTC and ETH establish sustained higher closes while ETH/BTC strength persists and participation broadens into positive median returns across large- and mid-alt proxies.
Newer settled flows and liquidity observations show improving demand alongside price recovery, rather than recovery occurring against continued contraction.
missing_evidence: No multi-session sequence demonstrates whether the current selling and breadth weakness are persisting or reversing.
More recent settled ETF sessions, repeated liquidity observations and deployment evidence are needed to assess demand over this horizon.
supporting_evidence: Stablecoin supply declined approximately 1.09% over seven days and 5.35% over 30 days, providing an observed liquidity headwind rather than evidence of expanding demand.
BTC and ETH 24h returns were approximately -1.86% and -1.51%, accompanied by negative aggregate and capitalization-proxy median returns.
The small-alt proxy's positive equal-weight mean contrasts with its negative median and only 30.4% advancing share; extreme individual gains do not demonstrate broad expansion.
Latest price-down/open-interest-up behavior adds near-term fragility, although it is not sufficient by itself to establish a multi-day decline.
